info.description:
GopherCRM is a self-hosted CRM: users, leads, customers, companies, deals, products, quotes, tickets, tasks, labels, follow-up automation, notifications, embeddable lead-capture forms and answer-engine visibility tracking (AEO). Every operation in this reference lives under the base path /api/v1 (configurable through API_PREFIX). GET /health is served outside the base path and is deliberately not part of this reference.

## Authentication
Protected operations accept one credential in the Authorization header, either `Authorization: Bearer <jwt>` (an access token from POST /auth/login or POST /auth/refresh) or `Authorization: ApiKey <key>` (a personal key from POST /api-keys; the plaintext key is shown once, at creation, and the gcrm_ prefix may be sent or left off). No other header, query parameter or cookie is read. A missing header, or one that is neither form, is 401 UNAUTHORIZED "Missing or invalid authorization header"; an invalid or expired credential, or one whose account is deactivated or erased, is 401 UNAUTHORIZED "Invalid credentials".
Login returns an access token (valid for JWT_EXPIRY_HOURS, 24 hours by default), a single-use refresh token (valid for REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY_DAYS, 30 days by default) and the user. POST /auth/refresh rotates strictly: the presented refresh token is spent and replaced, a spent token is refused with 401, and of several concurrent refreshes of one token exactly one succeeds, so a client must keep the replacement from every response. Logout, POST /auth/change-password and password reset revoke refresh tokens (a password changed through PUT /users/me revokes none), but an issued access token cannot be revoked early: it stays valid until it expires. Registration is open only while the security.allow_public_registration setting is on (it ships off), always creates a customer and returns an access token without a refresh token.
Roles are admin, sales, support and customer. Each operation names the roles it admits; another role gets 403 FORBIDDEN "Insufficient permissions". Where a role sees only some records (for example sales and its own leads), the operation describes the narrowing and the status a record outside it is answered with.

## Response envelope
Every JSON response has the shape {success, data, error, meta}. success is true for a 2xx response; data carries the payload (its shape is documented per operation); error is present only on failures; meta always carries request_id and, on paginated lists, page, per_page, total and total_pages (zero values are omitted, so an empty page has no total). A 204 response has no body.
Exceptions that are not enveloped: GET /customers/export (text/csv), the public form pages GET /forms/public/embed.js (JavaScript), GET /forms/public/{key}/view and GET/POST /forms/public/confirm (HTML), a CORS rejection (a bare 403 with no body) and a path or method that no route matches (the router's plain-text 404 "404 page not found").

## Errors
error.code is the stable value to branch on; error.message is for people and may change. Shared codes:
- 400 VALIDATION_ERROR: a binding or field rule failed. error.details is usually an object mapping each failed field to a message; binding failures key it by the server-side Go field name (for example FirstName), while service-level field checks use the JSON name. Operations that send another shape document it (a lead conversion rule sends {field}, plus status and allowed_statuses for a refused status; POST /aeo/prompts/{id}/run with an invalid id sends a plain string), and some omit details. A body over the public form submission limit is 413 with this code.
- 400 BAD_REQUEST: malformed JSON ("Invalid request format"), typically an unparsable path id, or another request the handler refuses as a whole.
- 400 INVALID_INPUT and INVALID_REFERENCE: a rule the service checks beyond the binding (automation rules, bulk status requests), or an id that names no live record (for example company_id, label_ids, a quote line's product).
- 401 UNAUTHORIZED: missing, malformed, invalid or expired credentials.
- 403 FORBIDDEN: the role is not admitted, or the record belongs to someone else where the operation says so.
- 404 NOT_FOUND: no live record with that id within the caller's visibility. Erased (soft-deleted) records are never returned.
- 409 CONFLICT and SESSION_STALE: a duplicate (email, domain, label name), a refused state change, or a stale session on a password change.
- INVALID_STATUS_TRANSITION: a refused status change; 400 for a quote transition, 409 for cancelling an automation run that has already finished.
- 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS: see Rate limits.
- 500 INTERNAL_ERROR: an unexpected failure ("An unexpected error occurred"); details are logged server-side, never returned.
- 502 MAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED (sending a quote by email), 503 SESSION_REFRESH_UNAVAILABLE (refresh), 503 PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED, PROVIDER_REJECTED, PROVIDERS_UNAVAILABLE and SHUTTING_DOWN (AEO).
Each operation lists the codes it can return and the condition behind each.

## Pagination, sorting and filtering
List operations take offset (default 0; negative or non-numeric values become 0) and limit (default 20; 0, negative or non-numeric values become 20; values above 100 are clamped to 100). Some lists also take a 1-based page that, when present, overrides offset. Out-of-range values are clamped or replaced, never rejected. Sortable lists accept sort_by from a fixed per-entity column list and sort_order asc or desc; what an unknown value does (ignored, defaulted or refused) is documented per operation.

## Rate limits
Requests are counted per client IP (the direct peer address unless TRUSTED_PROXIES names the proxy in front) in three tiers, each with its own buckets: strict, 10 requests per minute with a burst of 5, on every unauthenticated /auth route and on public form submission and confirmation; authenticated, 120 per minute with a burst of 30, shared by every authenticated operation and counted after authentication; generous, 240 per minute with a burst of 40, on public form reads. An exceeded limit is 429 TOO_MANY_REQUESTS with error.details {"retry_after": "60s"}, a fixed hint rather than the real wait. No Retry-After or X-RateLimit-* header is sent. Preflight OPTIONS requests are not counted.

## CORS and headers
Browser requests are admitted only from the configured origins (localhost development origins plus CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS), with credentials allowed, the methods GET, POST, PUT, PATCH, DELETE and OPTIONS and the request headers Origin, Content-Type, Authorization and X-Request-ID. A request from any other origin is refused with a bare 403 before any handler or log line. The public form endpoints under /forms/public answer any origin without credentials (methods GET, POST and OPTIONS, request header Content-Type).
Every response except a CORS preflight answer or a CORS rejection carries X-Request-ID: the value the client sent in that header, otherwise a generated UUID. The same value is meta.request_id in the envelope. Browsers on the configured origins can read X-Request-ID and Content-Length (exposed headers); the public form endpoints expose no headers, so a cross-origin page reads the id from meta.request_id instead.

Which sources the non-error answers cite over the requested window: the owned-domain citation rate, per-company citation and brand-mention rates (the brand first, then each competitor in profile order, companies without citations included) and the twenty most cited hosts by citation count descending. Windows are 7, 30 or 90 days; anything else falls back to 30. Works before a brand profile exists (by_company is then empty).
Roles: admin, sales, support.

put.description:
Save the single brand profile; the first call creates it, later calls replace it wholesale (a list left out of the body is cleared). The service trims every value, drops blank aliases, domains and competitors, de-duplicates aliases and domains case-insensitively, and reduces domains to bare lower-case hosts (scheme, path and a leading "www." removed). The response is the stored row. Only answers collected after the save are analysed against the new profile; stored answers keep their mention and citation analysis.
Roles: admin, sales.

Add 1 to 25 prompts in one request; new prompts are always active. Texts are trimmed and must be 1 to 500 characters. The batch is all-or-nothing and runs in one transaction: a repeat within the request or a text matching a live prompt (case-insensitive; soft-deleted prompts do not reserve their text) saves nothing and answers 409 CONFLICT, and so does nothing when the batch would push the number of active prompts above 100 (400). post.description:
Ask the generation engine for buyer-style questions derived from the brand profile. The engine is the integration.aeo.generation_engine setting (default anthropic; openai, gemini, kimi or perplexity are the other choices) and generation never falls back to another engine. Its API key is read from the admin settings first and from the engine's environment variable otherwise (ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, GEMINI_API_KEY, MOONSHOT_API_KEY, PERPLEXITY_API_KEY). The call is bounded by a 90-second timeout. Nothing is stored: the suggestions come back as plain strings (de-duplicated, each 12 to 500 characters, at most count of them) and are only tracked once POSTed to /aeo/prompts. The body is optional; an empty body asks for 10.
Side effects: one billed request to the external engine.
Roles: admin, sales.
Errors: 400 VALIDATION_ERROR (message "Validation failed", error.details maps the failing Go struct field name, e.g. BrandName or Prompts[0], to a message) when a binding rule fails; 400 BAD_REQUEST ("Invalid request format") for a body that is not valid JSON or does not match the field types; 409 CONFLICT when the brand profile has not been configured; 503 PROVIDER_NOT_CONFIGURED when the selected engine has no API key (the message names the engine); 503 PROVIDER_REJECTED when the engine answered with an HTTP error ("the generation engine rejected the request (HTTP 401) — check its API key in the AEO settings" for a 4xx, "the generation engine is unavailable (HTTP 529); try again later" otherwise). 503 rather than 502 so the JSON body survives proxies such as Cloudflare. A failure without an HTTP status (timeout, DNS, TLS, egress policy) and an answer with no usable suggestion are 500 INTERNAL_ERROR.

Any authenticated role, through a bearer token or an existing API key; the key always belongs to the caller. The plaintext key (gcrm_ followed by 64 hexadecimal characters) is returned only in this response: only an HMAC of it is stored, so it can never be shown again. Use it as `Authorization: ApiKey <key>`; the gcrm_ prefix may be sent or left off. The key acts with the owner's role and stops working when it is revoked, when it expires, or when the owner is deactivated or erased.
expires_at is optional: an RFC 3339 timestamp (for example 2026-12-31T23:59:59Z) that must lie in the future; omitted or empty, the key never expires. Expiry cannot be changed afterwards. There is no limit on the number of keys per user.

post.description:
Any authenticated role. Re-authenticates with current_password, then replaces it with new_password (at least 10 characters with an uppercase letter, a lowercase letter, a digit and a special character). The password write, the revocation of the caller's refresh tokens and the renewal of the current session are one transaction: a failure before the commit leaves the password and every session unchanged. A COMMIT whose acknowledgement fails is ambiguous (the change may have been applied) and is reported as a 500 without credentials. The login lockout counter is not touched.
With a bearer token and the client's current refresh_token in the body, that session is renewed: the token is spent, every other refresh token of the caller is revoked, and the response carries a replacement token, refresh_token and user. A refresh_token that is not a live session of the caller (unknown, revoked, expired, foreign) is 409 SESSION_STALE and nothing changes. Without a refresh_token, or for an API-key request (whose refresh_token is ignored and which never receives session credentials), every refresh token is revoked and only the message is returned.
Revocation ends renewal, not access: access tokens already issued stay valid until they expire (there is no blocklist). A wrong current password is a 400, not a 401, because the request itself is authenticated. Rate limit: the authenticated tier (120 per minute, burst 30, per client IP).

delete.description:
Admin only (route guard, repeated in the handler); an admin cannot erase its own account. This is a GDPR Article 17 erasure and cannot be undone: in one transaction every personal field is overwritten in place (the email becomes a random address in the reserved .invalid domain, the names are blanked, the password hash is made unusable, is_active becomes false and the login bookkeeping is cleared), the user's API keys, refresh tokens, password-reset tokens and notifications are deleted, the bodies of the ticket comments the user wrote become [deleted], and the row is soft-deleted. The row is kept so references from tickets, tasks, leads and deals still resolve, and the original email becomes free for a new account.
Erasing a customer-role user also erases, in the same transaction, every customer record whose user_id is that login and every lead converted into those customers. Erasing a staff user leaves the records it owns, manages or is assigned to untouched. To suspend an account reversibly use POST /users/{id}/deactivate instead.

Not populated by the API-key endpoints: always serialised as an empty
placeholder user object (id 0, every string empty, role "" included),
so it is documented as a plain object rather than a User. Use user_id.

user_id.description: ID of the owning user, always the account that created the key. Read-only.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: The simulated outcome of an automation rule (or an unsaved draft) against one record. Nothing is written, sent or notified.

draft.description: True when an unsaved rule body was simulated (POST /automation/rules/dry-run).

entity_id.description: ID of the record simulated against.

entity_type.description: Kind of the record simulated against.

rule_id.description: ID of the simulated rule; 0 for a draft.

rule_version.description: Version of the simulated rule; 0 for a draft.

simulated_end.description: The simulated end (RFC 3339, UTC): the start plus every wait that was reached.

simulated_start.description: The simulated start (RFC 3339, UTC): the time of the request.

steps.description: The steps that would run, in execution order; always an array, possibly empty.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: One line of a dry-run report: what a step would do, at the simulated time. Nothing in it was written.

details.description: What the step would touch, by step type: wait resume_at; condition result, branch (next, jump or stop) and next_position for a jump; create_task assignee_id, due_date and lead_id or customer_id; assign_owner from_owner_id and to_owner_id; send_email and notify recipient_id. Always an object, possibly empty.

error_code.description: recipient_unavailable when the step would be skipped; omitted otherwise.

outcome.description: Would-be result: succeeded, waiting (a wait step; the simulated clock moves on), or skipped when no active staff recipient or owner is available.

position.description: 1-based position of the step. Steps skipped by a condition branch do not appear.

simulated_at.description: The simulated time the step would run at (RFC 3339, UTC): the dry run's start plus every earlier wait.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: An admin-defined follow-up rule: a lead or deal trigger (or a daily UTC schedule) and up to 20 ordered steps.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

created_by_id.description: ID of the admin who created the rule; omitted when unknown. Read-only.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

description.description: Free-text description for admins, at most 65535 bytes; an empty string when none.
description.example: Creates a call-back task for every lead from the website.

enabled.description: Whether the rule starts new runs. A new rule is disabled unless the create body sends true; a PUT without enabled keeps the stored value.

entity_type.description: Kind of record the rule runs on.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

name.description: Rule name, trimmed, 1 to 200 characters.

schedule_completed_on.description: Schedule rules: the UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD) whose pass last finished; omitted when none. Server-maintained, read-only.

schedule_cursor.description: Schedule rules: the last record id handed out in the pass in progress; 0 otherwise. Server-maintained, read-only.

schedule_pass_on.description: Schedule rules: the UTC day (YYYY-MM-DD) of the pass in progress; omitted when none. Server-maintained, read-only.

steps.description: The ordered steps, by position (1 to 20 of them). Replaced wholesale, with new ids, by every PUT.

trigger.description: The trigger configuration; which fields apply depends on trigger_type.

trigger_type.description: What starts a run. Lead rules take lead_created, lead_updated, lead_status_changed or schedule; deal rules take deal_created, deal_updated, deal_stage_changed or schedule. Writes made by an automation step never start a run.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

version.description: Starts at 1 and is incremented by every PUT /automation/rules/{id} (enabling or disabling does not change it); every run records the version it started from. Read-only.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: One execution of an automation rule against one lead or deal. It never carries the rule's trigger or steps, only the rule's name.

attempts.description: Step attempts that failed or were released so far (never reset). An attempt that fails with attempts already at 2 fails the run with error_code step_failed. Read-only.

cancel_reason.description: Why a cancelled run was cancelled: the rule was changed, disabled or deleted, an admin cancelled it (manual), or the record was deleted. Omitted unless the run is cancelled. Read-only.

claimed_at.description: When an executor last claimed the run (RFC 3339); omitted when not set. Read-only.

created_at.description: When the run was started (RFC 3339). Read-only.

dedupe_key.description: Unique key that stops a run being started twice: evt:<event_id>:rule:<rule_id> for an event run, sch:<rule_id>:<YYYY-MM-DD>:<entity_id> for a schedule run. Read-only.

entity_id.description: ID of the lead or deal the run acts on. Read-only.

entity_type.description: Kind of record the run acts on. Read-only.

error_code.description: Why a failed run failed: step_failed (a step kept failing) or email_unconfirmed (an email may or may not have been sent and is never retried). Omitted unless the run failed. Read-only.

event_id.description: ID of the lead or deal event that started the run; omitted for a schedule run. Read-only.

finished_at.description: When the run reached completed, failed or cancelled (RFC 3339); omitted while it is active. Read-only.

id.description: Unique identifier of the run. Read-only.

next_position.description: 1-based position of the next step to execute. Read-only.

resume_at.description: When a waiting run resumes (RFC 3339); omitted when not set. Read-only.

rule_deleted.description: True when the rule has been deleted since (or is gone). Read-only.

rule_id.description: ID of the rule the run executes. Read-only.

rule_name.description: The rule's current name (also for a soft-deleted rule; empty when the rule row is gone), filled in by the run reads; it has no column. Read-only.

rule_version.description: The rule version the run was started from. Read-only.

status.description: Lifecycle status: pending (queued), running (an executor holds it), waiting (paused by a wait step until resume_at), and the final completed, failed and cancelled. Read-only.

steps.description: The step log, by position. Only returned by GET /automation/runs/{id} and POST /automation/runs/{id}/cancel; omitted from the list. Read-only.

updated_at.description: When the run row was last written (RFC 3339). Read-only.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: The log row of one executed step of a run. It holds ids, outcomes and error codes, never personal data.

details.description: Ids and statuses the step touched, never names or addresses. Keys by step type: wait resume_at; condition result, branch (next, jump or stop) and next_position for a jump; create_task assignee_id, due_date, lead_id or customer_id and task_id; assign_owner from_owner_id and to_owner_id; send_email and notify recipient_id, plus notification_id for notify. Always an object, possibly empty. Read-only.

error_code.description: Why the step was skipped or failed: recipient_unavailable (no active staff user to receive or own it), mail_failed (delivery failed; the run continues) or email_unconfirmed. Omitted otherwise. Read-only.

executed_at.description: When the step was executed (RFC 3339). Read-only.

id.description: Unique identifier of the log row. Read-only.

outcome.description: Result: succeeded, skipped (the recipient was unavailable), failed (the email could not be delivered, or was left unconfirmed), sending (an email is being handed to the mail relay) or waiting (a wait step paused the run). Read-only.

position.description: 1-based position of the executed step in the rule version the run started from. Read-only.

step_type.description: Type of the executed step. Read-only.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Narrows the records a schedule rule visits on each daily pass; an empty field is no filter.

stage.description: Deal rules only: visit only deals in this stage. Omitted or empty means any stage; set on a lead rule it is refused (invalid_value).

status.description: Lead rules only: visit only leads in this status. Omitted or empty means any status; set on a deal rule it is refused (invalid_value).

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: One ordered step of an automation rule.

config.description: The step configuration as stored, with defaults filled in (recipient owner, else stop); which fields apply depends on step_type.

created_at.description: When the step row was written (RFC 3339). Read-only.

id.description: Unique identifier of the step row. Read-only; a PUT of the rule replaces the steps with new ids.

position.description: 1-based position of the step in the rule, the order of the steps array in the request. Read-only.

rule_id.description: ID of the rule the step belongs to. Read-only.

step_type.description: What the step does: wait pauses the run, condition tests the record and stops or jumps when false, create_task creates a task, assign_owner changes the record's owner, send_email emails a staff user, notify creates an in-app notification.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Configuration of one automation step. Which fields apply depends on step_type: wait (duration_minutes), condition (field, operator, value, currency, else, else_position), create_task (title, description, priority, due_in_days, recipient, user_id), assign_owner (user_id), send_email (subject, body, recipient, user_id), notify (title, body, recipient, user_id).

body.description: send_email (required) and notify (optional): the body template, at most 65535 bytes, with the notify placeholders. An email is sent as plain text to the recipient's address.

currency.description: condition on amount_cents only: the ISO currency (three upper-case letters) the amount is in. Required for amount_cents and refused on any other field; a deal in another currency makes the condition false, amounts in different currencies are never compared.

description.description: create_task only: the task description template, at most 65535 bytes, with the task placeholders of title.
description.example: Lead status is {{ lead.status }}.

due_in_days.description: create_task only: the new task is due this many days after the step runs, 0 to 365.

duration_minutes.description: wait: how long the run pauses, in minutes, 1 to 129600 (90 days). The waits of one rule may add up to at most 90 days.

else.description: condition: what happens when the condition is false. stop ends the run; jump continues at else_position. Empty is stored as stop.

else_position.description: condition with else jump only: the 1-based position to continue at, which must come after the condition step and be at most the step count. Refused (not_applicable) with else stop.

field.description: condition: the record field compared. Lead rules: status, source, classification, company (compared as strings) and owner_id (a number). Deal rules: stage, source, currency (strings), amount_cents (money, needs currency) and probability, owner_id (numbers). Names, addresses and notes are never comparable.

operator.description: condition: the comparison. String fields take eq, neq, in, not_in, contains (case-insensitive substring), is_empty and is_not_empty; number and money fields take eq, neq, gt, gte, lt and lte.

priority.description: create_task only: the new task's priority; empty means medium.

recipient.description: create_task, send_email, notify: who receives the task, the email or the notification. owner is the record's owner at execution time; user is the staff user named by user_id. Empty is stored as owner. assign_owner always stores user.

subject.description: send_email only (required): the subject template, at most 255 characters and no line break, with the notify placeholders.

title.description: create_task and notify (required): the title template, at most 255 characters and no line break. Placeholders are written as {{ name }}. A notify title may use lead.id, lead.first_name, lead.last_name, lead.email, lead.phone, lead.company, lead.status, lead.source (lead rules) or deal.id, deal.title, deal.stage, deal.amount, deal.currency, deal.source (deal rules), plus owner.first_name, owner.last_name, owner.email; a task title only lead.id, lead.status, lead.source (lead rules) or the deal placeholders (deal rules).

user_id.description: The staff user (active, not a customer) named by recipient user, and the new owner of an assign_owner step, where it is required. Refused (not_applicable) with recipient owner. An unknown, deactivated or customer user is refused with unknown_reference (400 INVALID_REFERENCE when it is the first refusal).

value.description: condition: the value compared against, as raw JSON whose type depends on the operator: a string for eq/neq/contains on a string field, a non-empty array of strings for in/not_in, a number for every operator on a number or money field (amount_cents in minor units), and no value (omitted or null) for is_empty/is_not_empty. The schema therefore names no type; an object is always refused.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Trigger configuration of an automation rule. from and to apply to status or stage change triggers; hour_utc, filters and stale_days to the schedule trigger.

filters.description: Schedule trigger only: narrows the records each pass visits. Refused (not_applicable) on an event trigger.

from.description: Only for lead_status_changed and deal_stage_changed: start only when the previous value was this lead status (lead rules) or deal stage (deal rules). Omitted or empty means any; on any other trigger type it is refused (not_applicable).

hour_utc.description: Schedule trigger only: the UTC hour (0-23) from which the daily pass may start; it starts at the first worker tick at or after that hour. Always present in responses (0 for event triggers); a non-zero value on an event trigger is refused (not_applicable).

stale_days.description: Schedule trigger only: visit only records whose updated_at is more than this many days old; 0 or omitted means any age. Must not be negative; refused (not_applicable) on an event trigger.

to.description: Only for lead_status_changed and deal_stage_changed: start only when the new value is this lead status (lead rules) or deal stage (deal rules). Omitted or empty means any; on any other trigger type it is refused (not_applicable).

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Result of an all-or-nothing bulk status update: every listed record was updated.

updated.description: Number of records updated: the count of distinct ids in the request (a repeated id is updated once).

country.description: Country, free text, at most 100 characters.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

customer_count.description:
Number of live customers linked to the company. Computed by the company
endpoints; 0 where the company is embedded in another record (a lead's
company_record, a deal's company). Read-only.

deal_count.description:
Number of live deals linked to the company, whoever owns them. Computed
like customer_count. Read-only.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

domain.description:
Normalised domain: lower case, without scheme, path, query, a leading
"www." or a trailing dot. Empty when not set. Unique among live
(not deleted) companies.

employee_range.description: Head-count band, or empty when unknown.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

industry.description: Industry, free text, at most 100 characters; may be empty.

lead_count.description:
Number of live leads linked to the company, whoever owns them. Computed
like customer_count. Read-only.

name.description: Company name, trimmed, 1 to 200 characters. Required.

notes.description: Free-text notes, at most 65535 bytes (UTF-8 bytes, not characters).

owner.description:
The account manager's user record, loaded by the company endpoints;
omitted when unowned or when the owner account no longer exists.

owner_id.description: Account manager (a user id). Omitted when the company is unowned.

phone.description: Switchboard phone number, free text, at most 50 characters.

state.description: State or region, at most 100 characters.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

website.description: Website as entered (trimmed); an http or https URL, or empty.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Category a configuration entry is listed under.

Declared type of a configuration entry: it decides which JSON values PUT /configurations/{key} accepts (string: a JSON string; boolean: true/false; integer: a whole number; float, json, array: any JSON value, stored as JSON text) and how value is encoded.
A customer: a person the business serves, created directly or by converting a lead. Deleting one erases its personal data in place (GDPR Article 17).

assigned_to.description:
The account named by assigned_to_id. Not embedded by the customer
endpoints; absent unless an endpoint loads it.

assigned_to_id.description:
ID of the staff account that manages the relationship; absent while
unassigned. Set by POST /customers/{id}/assign (admin or sales accounts
only) or, when leads.conversion.auto_assign_owner is on, by a lead
conversion to the lead's owner.

company.description: Free-text company name as entered; independent of company_id.

company_id.description:
ID of the linked company record; absent when the customer has no link.
Independent of the free-text company field.

company_record.description:
The company named by company_id, embedded only by some reads (for
example GET /customers/{id}); absent otherwise.

country.description: Country, free text (no code list is enforced).

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

email.description:
Email address, unique among all customers, erased ones included (409 on
a duplicate). Required on create.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

notes.description:
Free-text notes. A lead conversion stores the notes sent with the
conversion request here.

phone.description: Phone number, free text; "" when unknown.

state.description: State, county or region, free text.

tickets.description:
Tickets of the customer. Not embedded by the customer endpoints (use
GET /customers/{id}/tickets); absent unless an endpoint loads them.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

user.description:
The login named by user_id, embedded only by some reads (for example
GET /customers/{id}); absent otherwise.

user_id.description:
ID of the customer's own login (a user account), if any; absent when
none. No API operation sets it. When it names a customer-role account,
erasing either erases both. Read-only.

website.description:
Web site: "" or an absolute http/https URL of at most 255 characters,
trimmed by the server.

amount_cents.description:
Deal value in minor units of currency (cents for EUR), an integer from
0 to 1000000000000 (10^12). Sums are meaningful per currency only.

closed_at.description:
When the deal entered won or lost (UTC, RFC 3339). Set by the server on
entering a closed stage, cleared on returning to an open one; omitted
while the deal is open. Read-only.

company.description:
The linked company, loaded by the deal endpoints (its customer_count,
lead_count and deal_count are 0 here, not computed). Omitted when there
is no link or the company no longer exists.

company_id.description:
Linked company. Omitted when there is none; cleared when the company
is deleted.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 code: exactly three upper-case ASCII letters. Defaults to the
deals.default_currency setting (EUR as shipped) on create.

customer.description:
The linked customer, loaded by the deal endpoints; omitted when there
is no link or the customer was erased (soft-deleted).

customer_id.description:
Linked customer. Omitted when there is none. Erasing the customer
keeps the link.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

expected_close_date.description:
Expected close date as a calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD (no time, no zone).
Omitted when not set.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

lead.description: The linked lead, under the same visibility rule as lead_id.

lead_id.description:
Linked lead. Omitted when there is none AND whenever the caller may not
see that lead (admins see every lead, sales users only the leads they
own); decided on every read.

lost_reason.description:
Why the deal was lost, at most 255 characters. Kept only while the
stage is lost; empty otherwise.

notes.description: Free-text notes, at most 65535 bytes (UTF-8 bytes, not characters).
notes.example: Decision expected after the board meeting.

owner.description: The owner's user record, loaded by the deal endpoints.

owner_id.description:
Staff user working the deal. Never null: defaults to the caller; only
an admin may name somebody else. Sales users see only their own deals.

probability.description:
Win probability in percent, 0 to 100. Takes the stage's default when a
stage is entered without an explicit value (qualification 10, proposal
40, negotiation 70); won is always 100 and lost always 0.

source.description: Where the deal came from, free text, at most 100 characters.

stage.description:
Pipeline stage. Defaults to qualification on create. Every change is
recorded in the stage history (GET /deals/{id}/history).

title.description: Deal title, trimmed, 1 to 200 characters. Required.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

stages.description:
The pipeline stages, exactly as GET /deals/pipeline returns them for
the caller (a sales user's own deals only).

won_this_month.description:
Deals whose closed_at falls in the current calendar month (UTC) and
that are in the won stage, for the same owner scope.

stages.description:
All five stages in pipeline order (qualification, proposal,
negotiation, won, lost), empty ones included.

count.description: Number of live (not deleted) deals in the stage, over all currencies.

stage.description:
The stage this entry aggregates. The five stages always appear, in
pipeline order.

totals.description:
One total per currency, sorted by currency code; an empty array, never
null, when the stage holds no deal.

amount_cents.description:
Sum of amount_cents of the stage's live deals in this currency, in
minor units.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 code of this total; one entry per currency present in the
stage.

weighted_cents.description:
Probability-weighted amount in minor units: round_half_up(sum of
amount_cents x probability / 100), integer arithmetic, rounded once on
the sum, never per deal.

changed_at.description: When the change was written (UTC, RFC 3339).

changed_by.description:
The acting user's full record (including email), loaded by GET
/deals/{id}/history; omitted when that account no longer exists.

deal_id.description: The deal this row belongs to.

from_stage.description:
Stage before the change; null on the first row, written when the deal
was created.

id.description: History row id, increasing in write order.

count.description: Number of deals won in the period, over all currencies.

totals.description:
The amounts won per currency, sorted by currency code; an empty array,
never null, when nothing was won.

amount_cents.description:
Sum of amount_cents of the deals won in the period in this currency,
in minor units.

allowed_domains.description:
Origin allowlist: bare host names with an optional port, lower-cased,
matched exactly (subdomains must be listed one by one). Empty allows
every origin. A definition requested from another origin is a 404; a
submission from another origin is stored as spam (reason domain). At
most 20, each at most 255 characters. Reads return [] when there are
none; the POST /forms and PUT /forms/{id} responses echo the request and
carry null when the list was omitted or sent as null.

captcha_enabled.description:
Require a reCAPTCHA v3 token with each submission. Takes effect only
when the server has both reCAPTCHA keys; otherwise it is ignored.

confirmation_subject.description:
Subject of the confirmation mail, at most 255 characters; empty means
"Confirm your email address".

consent_text.description:
Consent statement shown with the form. When non-empty, a submission must
carry consent=true or it is rejected with a field error on "consent".
consent_text.example: I agree to be contacted about my enquiry.

content_url.description:
Link inserted for {content_link} in the follow-up mail (for gated
content). At most 512 characters; not checked for a scheme.

create_lead.description:
Whether an accepted submission feeds a lead: the newest live lead with
the same address gains a note, otherwise a new lead (status new, owner
default_owner_id, source the form name) is created.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

created_by_id.description: ID of the user who created the form; server-assigned and immutable.

default_owner_id.description:
Owner of the leads the form creates; 0 means none. Required when
create_lead is true; any non-zero value names an active admin or sales
user (checked on save only).

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

description.description: Internal description for staff; never exposed by the public endpoints.
description.example: Contact form on the pricing page.

double_opt_in.description:
Double opt-in: a submission is stored as pending and a confirmation
mail with a single-use link valid for 48 hours goes to the submitted
address; the lead, the notification and the follow-up mail wait until
the link is confirmed.

fields.description:
Ordered field definitions (1 to 50), normalised on save (names trimmed,
max_length defaulted and clamped).

follow_up_body.description:
Plain-text body of the follow-up mail; {content_link} is replaced by
content_url. Empty means a built-in text containing the link.
follow_up_body.example: Thanks for your interest. Download the guide here: {content_link}

follow_up_subject.description:
Subject of the follow-up mail sent to the submitter once the submission
is accepted; empty means no follow-up mail is sent. At most 255
characters.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

name.description:
Form name, trimmed; at most 255 characters. Shown to visitors, used as
the source of the leads the form creates (cut to 100 characters) and in
notification subjects.

notify_emails.description:
Staff addresses that receive one notification mail per accepted
submission (on arrival, or on confirmation for double opt-in forms). At
most 20, each at most 255 characters and shaped like an address; trimmed.
Reads return [] when there are none; the POST /forms and PUT /forms/{id}
responses echo the request and carry null when the list was omitted or
sent as null.

public_id.description:
Public identifier used in every public URL (/forms/public/{key}): 22
random URL-safe base64 characters assigned at creation and never changed,
so embeds keep working across edits.

status.description:
Publication state; only a published form is served by the public
endpoints. Defaults to draft.

submit_action.description:
What the visitor sees after submitting: message shows thank_you_message
in place, redirect sends the browser to redirect_url. Defaults to
message.

thank_you_message.description:
Message shown after a submission when submit_action is message. When
empty a default text is shown (a "check your inbox" text for double
opt-in forms).
thank_you_message.example: Thanks, we will be in touch within one business day.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

help_text.description: Help text rendered under the input; omitted when empty.
help_text.example: We only use this to reply to you.

label.description:
Label shown to the visitor and used in validation messages and lead
notes; the name is used when it is empty.

max_length.description:
Longest accepted value in characters. On save, 0 or absent becomes 1000
(5000 for textarea), anything above 10000 becomes 10000, and lead-mapped
fields are narrowed to their column: email 255, first_name and last_name
100, phone 50, company 200, position 100. Stored definitions therefore
always carry the enforced limit.

name.description:
Machine name: the input name, the key of the submitted value and, for
first_name, last_name, name, email, phone, company and position, the lead
column it fills. Must match ^[a-z][a-z0-9_]{0,49}$ (trimmed first) and be
unique within the form. The one email field must be named "email".

options.description:
Choices of a select field (1 to 50, none blank); the submitted value must
equal one of them exactly. Omitted for other types, which may not have
options.

placeholder.description: Placeholder text for the input; omitted when empty.

required.description: Whether a value must be submitted; for a checkbox, that it is ticked.

type.description:
Input type. A form has exactly one field of type email. Only select may
have options; hidden carries a prefilled value and cannot be required.

confirmed_at.description: When the double opt-in link was confirmed (RFC 3339); null otherwise.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

data.description:
Submitted values keyed by field name: every field of the definition is
present, values are trimmed, checkboxes are "true" or "false" and the
email is lower-cased. Emptied ({}) when the linked lead is erased.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

email.description:
Submitted address, lower-cased. After erasure of the linked lead it is
that lead's placeholder address.

form_id.description: ID of the form that was submitted.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

ip_address.description:
Client IP as resolved through the trusted proxies (TRUSTED_PROXIES).
Emptied when the linked lead is erased.

lead_id.description:
Lead the submission created or added a note to; null for spam and
pending submissions and for forms with create_lead off.

referrer.description:
Page the form was submitted from, as reported by the embed script
(page_url; client-supplied, not verified), cut to 512 characters.
Emptied when the linked lead is erased.

spam_reason.description:
Protection layer that caught a spam submission: time_trap (submitted
under 3 seconds or over 24 hours after the definition was served),
domain (origin not in allowed_domains), honeypot (decoy input filled) or
captcha (token missing, rejected or unverifiable). Empty string for every
other status.

status.description:
Lifecycle state: received (final on arrival), pending (double opt-in
confirmation outstanding), confirmed (link confirmed) or spam (caught by
a protection layer).

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

user_agent.description:
Browser User-Agent header, cut to 255 characters. Emptied when the
linked lead is erased.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: A coloured tag that can be attached to tasks. Labels are hard-deleted.

color.description: Colour as #RRGGBB (six hex digits behind a hash).

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

name.description: Display name, trimmed, 1 to 50 characters and unique case-insensitively.

task_count.description:
Number of live (not soft-deleted) tasks carrying the label, computed on
read and never stored. Filled in by GET /labels and PUT /labels/{id}; 0
in the POST /labels response and in labels embedded in a task. Read-only.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

classification.description: Triage classification; unclassified when not set.

company.description:
Free-text employer name as typed or submitted by a form, independent of
company_id. The column holds 200 characters; the API does not check the
length.

company_id.description:
Curated company the lead is linked to, independent of the free-text
company field. Omitted when there is no link. Erasure and conversion
keep it; deleting the company clears it.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

customer.description:
The converted customer. The lead endpoints never load it, so it is
omitted.

customer_id.description:
Customer this lead was converted into. Set by POST /leads/{id}/convert,
read-only otherwise; omitted while the lead is unconverted.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

email.description:
Email address, validated as an address when sent. Empty when the lead
was created with a phone number only (a create needs an email or a
phone). Not unique: one person may be captured more than once. Erasure
replaces it with a random address in the reserved .invalid domain.

external_id.description:
Identifier of the lead in an external system (imports). Omitted when
empty; not unique.

first_name.description:
Given name. Required on create (any non-empty string); an update
cannot clear it. The column holds 100 characters; the API does not
check the length.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

last_name.description:
Family name. Required on create; an update cannot clear it. The column
holds 100 characters; the API does not check the length.

notes.description:
Free-text notes: staff text plus one block per public-form submission
from the lead's address (oldest form blocks are trimmed whole to stay
within the column). Writes through the API are refused above 65535
bytes (UTF-8 bytes, not characters).
notes.example: Met at the trade fair; wants a demo.

owner.description:
The owner's account. Always present in the JSON. GET /leads/{id}, the
admin GET /leads (except with the classification filter),
GET /leads?external_id= for admin and sales, GET /companies/{id}/leads and the dashboard fill it in with the User
object (see the User schema); elsewhere (create and update responses, a
sales user's list) it is a zero-valued placeholder (id 0, every string
empty, role "" included), which is not a valid User, so this property is
documented as a plain object. Use owner_id.

owner_id.description:
Staff user who owns the lead. A sales user sees and edits only the
leads it owns; only an admin may reassign a lead.

phone.description:
Phone number, free text, may be empty. The column holds 50 characters;
the API does not check the length.

position.description:
Job title, free text, may be empty (100-character column, not checked
by the API).

source.description:
Where the lead came from, free text (100-character column, not checked
by the API). Leads created by a public form carry the form's name.

status.description:
Pipeline status. Defaults to new on create. converted is set only by
POST /leads/{id}/convert; any other write that asks for it is refused.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: An in-app message for one staff user, created by the notify step of an automation rule.

body.description: Body rendered from the notify step's body template; an empty string when the step has no body.
body.example: Please contact the lead within one business day.

created_at.description: When the notification was created (RFC 3339). Read-only.

entity_id.description: ID of the lead or deal the notification is about.

entity_type.description: Type of the record the notification is about.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server. Read-only.

read_at.description: When the caller marked it read (RFC 3339); omitted while unread.

run_id.description: ID of the automation run that created the notification; omitted when there is none.

title.description: Title rendered from the notify step's title template (placeholders substituted), cut to 255 characters.

updated_at.description: When the row was last written (RFC 3339), e.g. when it was marked read. Read-only.

user_id.description: ID of the staff user the notification is addressed to; always the caller on these endpoints.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 code: exactly three upper-case ASCII letters. Defaults to the
deals.default_currency setting (EUR as shipped). A product can be added
only to quotes in the same currency.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

description.description:
Free-text description, at most 65535 bytes (UTF-8 bytes, not
characters). Not copied onto quote lines.
description.example: Business-hours support for twelve months.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

is_active.description:
Whether the product can be added to quote lines. Defaults to true on
create; existing lines of an inactive product are kept.

name.description:
Product name, trimmed, 1 to 200 characters. Copied onto a quote line
as its description when the line is added.

sku.description:
Optional stock-keeping code, trimmed, at most 64 characters; empty when
not set. Not unique.

unit_price_cents.description:
Price of one unit in minor units of currency (cents for EUR), 0 to
1000000000000 (10^12). 0 is a free item. Copied onto a quote line when
the line is added.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

id.description: Customer id.
Deal id.

closed_at.description:
When the quote was accepted, rejected or expired (UTC); cleared on sent
to draft. Omitted when not set. Read-only.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 code shared by every line: exactly three upper-case ASCII
letters. Defaults to the deals.default_currency setting (EUR as
shipped); can change only while the quote has no lines.

customer.description:
Display summary of the linked customer (never its contact details).
Omitted when the quote has no customer or the customer was erased.

customer_id.description:
Customer the quote is addressed to (the email recipient). Omitted when
there is none, which happens when the quote was created from a deal
without a customer.

deal.description:
Summary of the deal the quote grew from. Omitted when there is none or
the deal was deleted.

deal_id.description:
Deal the quote grew from; set on create only, never editable. Omitted
when there is none.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

discount_cents.description:
subtotal_cents minus total_cents: the money taken off by the per-line
discounts, in minor units. Computed; read-only.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

last_emailed_at.description:
When the quote was last emailed successfully (UTC). Omitted when never.
Read-only.

lines.description:
The priced lines ordered by position, then id. Present on the detail
and write responses; an empty array (never null) in lists, which do not
load lines.

notes.description:
Free-text notes, at most 65535 bytes (UTF-8 bytes, not characters).
Included in the quote email.

number.description:
Human-readable quote number: Q- followed by the id zero-padded to six
digits. Computed; read-only.

owner.description:
Summary of the owner (no email). Omitted when the owner account no
longer exists.

owner_id.description:
Staff user owning the quote. Defaults to the caller; only an admin may
name somebody else. Sales users see only their own quotes.

sent_at.description:
When the quote last moved draft to sent (UTC); cleared on sent to draft.
Omitted when not set. Read-only.

status.description:
Lifecycle status. Always draft on create; changed only through POST
/quotes/{id}/status.

subtotal_cents.description:
Sum of quantity x unit_price_cents over the lines, in minor units.
Computed by the server on every line change; read-only.

title.description: Quote title, trimmed, 1 to 200 characters. Required.

total_cents.description:
Sum of the lines' line_total_cents, in minor units, at most
1000000000000 (10^12). Computed; read-only.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

valid_until.description:
Last day the offer is valid, a calendar date YYYY-MM-DD. Omitted when
not set. Accepting the quote is refused once this date lies before
today (server's local date); expiry itself is never automatic.

created_at.description: When the line was added (UTC).

description.description:
Line text: the product name at the time the line was added unless
overridden. Trimmed, 1 to 255 characters.
description.example: Annual support plan

discount_bp.description: Per-line discount in basis points, 0 to 10000 (1250 = 12.5 percent).

id.description: Line id.

line_total_cents.description:
quantity x unit_price_cents x (10000 - discount_bp) / 10000, rounded half
up to a whole minor unit. Computed by the server; read-only.

position.description:
1-based display order. A new line gets the highest position plus one;
positions are not renumbered and need not be unique.

product.description: Never loaded by the quote endpoints, so always omitted.

product_id.description:
The product the line was priced from. The product may since have been
changed, deactivated or deleted; the line keeps its copies.

quote_id.description: The quote the line belongs to.

unit_price_cents.description:
Price per unit in minor units of the quote's currency, 0 to
1000000000000: the product's price at the time the line was added
unless overridden.

updated_at.description: When the line was last changed (UTC).

id.description: User id.

changed_at.description: When the change was written (UTC, RFC 3339).

changed_by.description:
Summary of the acting user (no email). Omitted when that account no
longer exists.

from_status.description:
Status before the change; null on the first row, written when the
quote was created.

id.description: History row id, increasing in write order.

quote_id.description: The quote this row belongs to.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: A to-do item assigned to one user, optionally linked to a lead or a customer (never both) and carrying labels.

assigned_to.description: The assignee's user record. Always present in the JSON. GET /tasks/{id}, PUT /tasks/{id}, GET /tasks/upcoming and the admin and label-filtered GET /tasks listings fill it in with the User object (see the User schema). POST /tasks, GET /tasks/my and the non-admin GET /tasks without label_id return a zero-valued placeholder instead (id 0, every string empty, role "" included, timestamps 0001-01-01T00:00:00Z), which is not a valid User, so this property is documented as a plain object. Use assigned_to_id.

assigned_to_id.description: ID of the user the task is assigned to. Non-admins may only create tasks for themselves and only admins may change it.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

customer.description: The linked customer. Only loaded by GET /tasks/{id} and PUT /tasks/{id} (and omitted from the PUT response when that request changed customer_id); omitted everywhere else.

customer_id.description: ID of the linked customer. Omitted when the task has no customer link. A task links a lead or a customer, never both.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

description.description: Free-text details; an empty string when none were given.
description.example: Customer asked for a quote on the 50-seat plan.

due_date.description: Due date and time (RFC 3339). Omitted when the task has no due date; once set it cannot be cleared through PUT /tasks/{id}.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

labels.description: Labels attached to the task. Omitted when the task has none, and not loaded (so omitted) by GET /tasks/upcoming. The embedded labels carry task_count 0.

lead.description: The linked lead, under the same visibility rule as lead_id: omitted whenever lead_id is omitted.

lead_id.description: ID of the linked lead. Omitted when the task has no lead link, and also when the caller may not see that lead (admins see every lead, sales users only the leads they own, every other role none); this is decided on every read. A task links a lead or a customer, never both.

priority.description: Priority; medium when not given on create.

status.description: Workflow status. New tasks always start as pending; a completed task cannot move to another status.

title.description: Short summary of the task. Always present. The column is 255 characters wide; the API does not check the length before the write.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Priority of a task; medium when not given on create.
Workflow status of a task. A new task always starts as pending; a completed task cannot be moved to any other status.
A support request raised for a customer and handled by a support or admin user.

assigned_to.description: The assignee's user record, loaded by the same endpoints that fill in customer; omitted elsewhere and when the ticket is unassigned.

assigned_to_id.description: ID of the assigned support or admin user. POST /tickets assigns the caller when it is not given. Omitted when the ticket is unassigned.

comments.description: The ticket's comments, oldest first, each with its author. Only loaded by GET /tickets/{id} and PUT /tickets/{id}; omitted elsewhere. Customer callers never receive internal notes here.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

customer.description: The customer record. Always present in the JSON. GET /tickets, GET /tickets/{id} and PUT /tickets/{id} fill it in with the Customer object (see the Customer schema); POST /tickets, GET /tickets/my and GET /customers/{id}/tickets return a zero-valued placeholder instead (id 0, every string empty, email "" included), which is not a valid Customer, so this property is documented as a plain object. Use customer_id.

customer_id.description: ID of the customer the ticket belongs to. Set on create and never changed by PUT /tickets/{id}.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

description.description: Full description of the problem. Required on create.
description.example: Since this morning the office printer no longer appears on the network.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

priority.description: Priority; medium when not given on create.

resolution.description: How the ticket was resolved; an empty string until someone sets it. PUT /tickets/{id} cannot clear it.
resolution.example: Rolled the printer back to the previous firmware.

status.description: Workflow status. New tickets always start as open; a closed ticket cannot move to another status.

title.description: Short summary of the ticket. Required on create. The column is 255 characters wide; the API does not check the length before the write.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: A comment on a ticket, or an internal note visible to staff only.

author.description: The author's user record. Omitted when the author's account has since been deleted.

author_user_id.description: ID of the staff user who wrote the comment (the caller of POST /tickets/{id}/comments).

body.description: The comment text, trimmed of surrounding whitespace.
body.example: Rolled back the firmware; waiting for the customer to confirm.

content.description: Read-only alias of body, kept for older clients.
content.example: Rolled back the firmware; waiting for the customer to confirm.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

is_internal.description: True for an internal note: visible to staff only, never returned to customer callers.

ticket_id.description: ID of the ticket the comment belongs to.

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

user.description: Read-only alias of author, kept for older clients.

user_id.description: Read-only alias of author_user_id, kept for older clients.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Priority of a ticket; medium when not given on create.
Workflow status of a ticket. A new ticket always starts as open; a closed ticket cannot be moved to any other status.
A login account: staff (admin, sales, support) or a customer's own login. The password hash and the failed-login counter are never returned.

created_at.description: When the record was created (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server. Read-only.

deleted_at.description: Soft-deletion time (RFC 3339 date-time) or null. Always present in the JSON. Reads exclude soft-deleted rows, so records returned by the API carry null here. Read-only.

email.description:
Login email address, unique among all accounts, including erased ones
(erasure replaces the address, which frees it for reuse).

id.description: Unique identifier, assigned by the server on creation. Read-only.

is_active.description:
False for a deactivated account: it cannot log in, and its bearer tokens and
API keys are rejected. Changed only by an admin.

last_login_at.description:
Time of the last successful password login (RFC 3339). Absent when the
account has never logged in. Server-maintained, read-only.

locked_until.description:
End of the login lockout set after 5 consecutive failed logins (15 minutes,
RFC 3339). Absent when no lock is recorded; it may lie in the past, since a
lapsed lock is cleared only by the next login attempt. Server-maintained,
read-only.

role.description: Role of the account; only an admin can change it (PUT /users/{id}, POST /users).

updated_at.description: When the record was last written (RFC 3339 date-time), set by the server on every update. Read-only.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Role of an account. It decides which operations and records the account may reach; every operation lists the roles it admits. Public registration always creates customer accounts.

challenge.description:
Signed time-trap token minted for this response. Send it back unchanged
as challenge with the submission; a submission sent less than 3 seconds
or more than 24 hours after it was issued is filed as spam.

consent_text.description:
Consent statement to show with a checkbox; when present the submission
must carry consent=true. Omitted when the form has none.
consent_text.example: I agree to be contacted about my enquiry.

fields.description:
Ordered field definitions; max_length is the limit the submission
validator enforces. Always an array.

name.description: Form name, for the heading the renderer shows.

public_id.description: Public identifier of the form (the {key} of the public URLs).

recaptcha_site_key.description:
reCAPTCHA v3 site key the renderer loads; present only when the form
enables reCAPTCHA and the server has both keys configured.

submit_action.description:
What to do after submitting: show a message or redirect. Defaults to
message.

captcha_token.description:
reCAPTCHA v3 token; needed only when the definition carried
recaptcha_site_key. Missing or failing tokens file the submission as
spam.

challenge.description:
The challenge from the definition response, unchanged. Required: a
missing or blank one is 400 VALIDATION_ERROR.

consent.description:
Whether the visitor accepted the consent text; must be true when the
form has consent text, ignored otherwise.

page_url.description:
URL of the page the form was submitted from, stored as the submission's
referrer (cut to 512 characters). Not verified.

values.description:
Submitted values keyed by field name. Only fields the definition
declares are allowed; missing optional fields count as empty. Values are
trimmed; checkbox values true, 1, on, yes or checked (any case) mean
ticked, anything else unticked.

website_url_confirm.description:
Honeypot input; must be absent or empty. A non-empty value files the
submission as spam.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: One refused field of an automation rule body.

code.description: Why it was refused: required (missing or blank), too_long, line_break (a title or subject with a line break), invalid_value (not an allowed value), out_of_range (a number outside its bounds, or waits adding up to more than 90 days), not_applicable (set where it does not apply), unknown_placeholder, too_many (more than 20 steps) or unknown_reference (an unknown, deactivated or customer user).

field.description: Path of the refused field in the request body: name, description, entity_type, trigger_type, trigger.from, trigger.to, trigger.hour_utc, trigger.stale_days, trigger.filters, trigger.filters.status, trigger.filters.stage, steps, steps[i].step_type or steps[i].config.<name>, with i the zero-based index in the steps array.

message.description: Human-readable explanation; it may quote the refused value.

action.description:
The form's submit action: show message in place, or redirect to
redirect_url.

message.description:
Text to show for the message action: the form's thank-you message, or a
default ("check your inbox" for double opt-in forms). Omitted for the
redirect action.
message.example: Thank you. Your submission has been received.

pending_confirmation.description:
True when the form uses double opt-in, so a confirmation mail has been
sent (also reported for submissions filed as spam, which get no mail).

redirect_url.description: Where to send the browser for the redirect action; omitted otherwise.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Error object of a failed request. code is the stable value to branch on; message is for people and may change.

code.description:
Stable machine-readable error code. Shared codes: VALIDATION_ERROR,
BAD_REQUEST, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, NOT_FOUND, CONFLICT,
TOO_MANY_REQUESTS, INTERNAL_ERROR, MAIL_DELIVERY_FAILED; operations
document their own additional codes (for example INVALID_REFERENCE,
SESSION_STALE, SESSION_REFRESH_UNAVAILABLE).

details.description:
Optional context; its JSON type depends on the code and the operation,
so the schema leaves it open. Usually an object: a binding failure
(VALIDATION_ERROR) maps each failed field to a message, keyed by the
server-side Go field name (for example "Email", "FirstName"), not the
JSON name; TOO_MANY_REQUESTS carries {"retry_after": "60s"}. Some
operations send another shape (for example a plain string on POST
/aeo/prompts/{id}/run with an invalid id) and document it; many errors
omit it.

message.description: Human-readable explanation. Not stable: do not parse it.

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Response metadata. request_id is always present; the pagination fields appear only on paginated list responses and, like every zero value here, are omitted when 0.

page.description: 1-based page number of this response (paginated lists only; omitted when 0).

per_page.description: Page size used for this response (paginated lists only; omitted when 0).

request_id.description:
Correlation id of the request: the client's X-Request-ID header when
sent, otherwise a server-generated UUID. Also returned in the
X-Request-ID response header.

total.description:
Total number of matching records (paginated lists only; omitted when
0, so an empty result carries no total).

total_pages.description: Number of pages at per_page (paginated lists only; omitted when 0).

github_com_florinel-chis_gophercrm_inter.description: Envelope of every JSON response (the CSV export and the public form pages are the exceptions). success tells the outcome; data carries the payload on success, error the failure on error; meta is always present.

data.description:
Operation-specific payload on success (each operation documents its
shape). Absent on errors and on successes without a payload.

error.description: Failure details; present only when success is false.

meta.description:
Request metadata, present on every enveloped response, with pagination
fields on paginated lists.

success.description: True for a 2xx response, false when error is set.

aliases.description:
Alternative spellings counted as mentions of this competitor: at most 20,
each at most 120 characters. Trimmed, blanks dropped and de-duplicated
case-insensitively on save.

domain.description:
Competitor website, at most 255 characters. Any form is accepted
("https://www.Globex.example/about") and stored as a bare lower-case host
without scheme, path or leading "www.".

name.description:
Competitor name; required, at most 120 characters. Trimmed on save; an
entry whose name is only whitespace is silently dropped.

internal_handler.Activity.description: One entry of the recent-activity feed, synthesised from lead, ticket and task rows (there is no activity table).

created_at.description: Event time (RFC 3339): created_at for lead_created and ticket_created, otherwise the record's updated_at, so a later edit moves the entry.

description.description: For lead events "First Last (Company) was added as a lead" or "... was converted to a customer" (Unnamed lead when the names are empty); for ticket and task events the record's title.
description.example: Ana Popescu (Acme SRL) was added as a lead

id.description: Stable id {entity}-{record id}-{event}, e.g. lead-42-created.

title.description: Fixed title per type: New lead, Lead converted, New ticket, Ticket resolved, Task completed.

user.description: The lead's owner or the ticket's or task's assignee.

internal_handler.ActivityUser.description: Account shown against an activity entry: the lead's owner or the ticket's or task's assignee. Always present; every field is zero-valued (id 0, empty strings) when the record has no such account.

first_name.description: Given name; "" when there is no account.

id.description: User id; 0 when there is no account.

last_name.description: Family name; "" when there is no account.

username.description: The account's email address (there is no username column); "" when there is no account.

user_id.description:
ID of the new account manager: an existing, active admin or sales user.
Required and non-zero.

internal_handler.AuthResponse.description: Session credentials returned by login, refresh and registration.

refresh_token.description:
Opaque single-use refresh token (43 URL-safe base64 characters) for
POST /auth/refresh, valid for REFRESH_TOKEN_EXPIRY_DAYS (30 days by
default). Absent on registration, and on a login whose refresh token could
not be stored (the login then succeeds with the access token only).

token.description:
Access token: an HS256-signed JWT (claims user_id, email, role, exp) valid
for JWT_EXPIRY_HOURS (24 hours by default). Send it as
`Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It cannot be revoked before it expires.

internal_handler.AutomationDraftDryRunRe.description: Body of POST /automation/rules/dry-run: an unsaved rule and the record to simulate it against.

entity_id.description: ID of the live lead or deal to simulate against (404 when it does not exist).

entity_type.description: Kind of the record to simulate against; must match rule.entity_type (400 INVALID_INPUT otherwise).

rule.description: The unsaved rule body, as for POST /automation/rules (enabled is ignored).

internal_handler.AutomationDryRunRequest.description: Body of POST /automation/rules/{id}/dry-run: the record to simulate the saved rule against.

entity_id.description: ID of the live lead or deal to simulate against (404 when it does not exist).

entity_type.description: Kind of the record to simulate against; must match the rule's entity_type (400 INVALID_INPUT otherwise).

internal_handler.AutomationRuleErrorDeta.description: error.details of a refused automation rule body.

fields.description: Every refused field, in the order the checks ran; each field appears once, with its first refusal.

internal_handler.AutomationRuleRequest.description: Body of POST /automation/rules and PUT /automation/rules/{id}, and the rule of a draft dry run. Validated by the service (400 INVALID_INPUT or INVALID_REFERENCE with error.details.fields), not by binding rules.

description.description: Optional description, at most 65535 bytes.
description.example: Creates a call-back task for every lead from the website.

enabled.description: Whether the rule starts runs. On create, absent or null means false; on update, absent or null keeps the stored value. Ignored by the draft dry run.

entity_type.description: Kind of record the rule runs on. Required; any other value is refused (invalid_value) and stops the remaining checks.

name.description: Rule name. Required: trimmed, 1 to 200 characters (refused with required or too_long).

steps.description: The ordered steps, 1 to 20; they are numbered 1..n in this order. Missing or more than 20 skips the per-step checks.

trigger.description: Trigger configuration: from and to for a status or stage change, hour_utc, filters and stale_days for a schedule.

trigger_type.description: What starts a run. Required. Lead rules take lead_created, lead_updated, lead_status_changed or schedule; deal rules deal_created, deal_updated, deal_stage_changed or schedule (anything else is invalid_value and skips the trigger checks).

internal_handler.AutomationStepRequest.description: One step of an automation rule body.

config.description: The step configuration; only the fields of the step type apply, and a field set where it does not apply may be refused (not_applicable).

step_type.description: What the step does; see models.AutomationStepConfig for the fields each type takes. An unknown type is refused (invalid_value).

lead_ids.description: IDs of the leads to update, 1 to 100, each positive. A repeated id is updated once.

status.description: The status to set on every listed lead. converted passes the binding but is always refused (400 VALIDATION_ERROR, details.field status), so it is not listed among the accepted values: conversion goes through POST /leads/{id}/convert.
The status to set on every listed task. A completed task cannot be moved to another status.
